top_story_title: Check Point confirms in-the-wild exploitation of PHP2Shell against Security Gateways, chained to root
top_story_summary: Check Point Research reports active, in-the-wild exploitation of PHP2Shell, a vulnerability in PHP that also affects Check Point Security Gateways. In the incidents it observed, the attacker used PHP2Shell for initial access and then a local privilege escalation vulnerability to obtain root and establish persistence on the appliance. No CVE identifier is given in the advisory text, so track it by name and by the fix date until the vendor publishes one.
top_actions: Inventory Check Point Security Gateway and Management systems and compare running build against the fixes published October 23rd; patch anything older, starting with internet-facing gateways.

For any gateway that was internet-facing and unpatched after October 23rd, assume pre-patch compromise: look for unexpected root shells, new local accounts, modified web resources and unusual timestamps in /var logs.
Rotate local admin credentials, API keys, certificates and VPN pre-shared keys on affected gateways after upgrading - a pre-patch compromise survives the upgrade.
Terminate active remote-access sessions and revoke session tokens on upgraded gateways; treat existing session cookies as potentially stolen.
Remove management access (HTTPS/SSH/API) from untrusted and internet-facing interfaces and restrict it to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network.
executive_summary: Check Point Research confirms active exploitation of PHP2Shell against unpatched Check Point Security Gateways, chained with a local privilege escalation to root and persistence; fixes shipped October 23rd, so this is patch latency, not a zero-day.
Palo Alto Networks published a batch of PSIRT advisories; the one to act on first is CVE-2026-0330, authenticated RCE in Panorama - a management platform outranks a single gateway.
Five of the PAN-OS items concern GlobalProtect (authorization bypass, user impersonation, privilege escalation), so internet-facing portals belong in the same change window.
None of the Palo Alto feed entries state affected or fixed versions. Do not plan an upgrade from the digest - open each advisory for the fixed-release table.
No collected item genuinely concerns AI on network devices in this window, so the AI section carries forward; the only AI-adjacent item is Check Point's FedRAMP expansion for its WAF.
key_actions: **Check Point** — Confirm the running version of every Security Gateway and Management server against the vendor's fixed-release table and schedule the upgrade in the change window, HA pair secondary first.

**Check Point** — Treat any internet-facing gateway left unpatched after October 23rd as potentially compromised and hunt before closing the ticket: unexpected outbound connections, new local accounts, modified web resources, unusual timestamps in /var logs.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Read the advisory for the affected and fixed Panorama versions, then schedule the upgrade; upgrade Panorama before the firewalls it manages.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Confirm Panorama's management interface is unreachable from the internet and from user VLANs; restrict it to a management VLAN or out-of-band network with an explicit ACL.

ai_defenses.what_it_does: Check Point's web application firewall, now included in the company's FedRAMP certification. The post positions it in front of government citizen self-service portals, connected APIs and workflows into which AI has been integrated, each of which it describes as a new entry point.

headlines.title: Security Advisory: Active Exploitation of PHP2Shell and Local Privilege Escalation
headlines.summary: Check Point Research confirms in-the-wild exploitation of PHP2Shell against unpatched Check Point Security Gateways, chained with local privilege escalation to root and persistence.

headlines.title: CVE-2026-0330 PAN-OS: Authenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) in Panorama (Severity: MEDIUM)
headlines.summary: Palo Alto Networks discloses CVE-2026-0330, an authenticated remote code execution flaw in Panorama, the platform that manages PAN-OS firewall fleets.

headlines.title: CVE-2026-0331 PAN-OS: Sensitive Information Disclosure Vulnerability (Severity: MEDIUM)
headlines.summary: CVE-2026-0331 is a sensitive information disclosure vulnerability in PAN-OS, rated medium by Palo Alto Networks, with no detail published in the advisory feed.

headlines.title: CVE-2026-0329 PAN-OS: Buffer Overflow Vulnerability (Severity: MEDIUM)
headlines.summary: CVE-2026-0329 is a buffer overflow in PAN-OS rated medium by Palo Alto Networks; the advisory feed entry carries no technical detail.

headlines.title: CVE-2026-0325 PAN-OS: GlobalProtect Authorization Bypass Vulnerability (Severity: LOW)
headlines.summary: CVE-2026-0325 is an authorization bypass vulnerability in GlobalProtect on PAN-OS, rated low by Palo Alto Networks but sitting on an internet-facing remote-access portal.

headlines.title: CVE-2026-0328 PAN-OS: User Impersonation through GlobalProtect Portal (Severity: LOW)
headlines.summary: CVE-2026-0328 lets an attacker impersonate another user through the GlobalProtect portal on PAN-OS; Palo Alto Networks rates it low.
